title: Sporadic fidelity docket
content:
Purpose: quick, messy notebook for intermittent fidelity observations and a tiny ad-hoc rubric I can reuse when pulling small samples. Not for publication — personal scratchpad.

Context: running periodic smoke checks on hosted-api model variants (gptx-small / gptx-small-quant) after the kernel selector changes. Observed a small cluster of low-confidence outputs on 1.3k-sample regression run dated 2025-01-04 (see JIRA-ML-1427). I want a reproducible one-pager I can copy into ticket notes.

1) Quick ad-hoc rubric (0-3 scale) — use for 20-sample spot checks:
- 0 = broken: answer irrelevant or contradicts prompt intent
- 1 = degraded: partially correct but misses explicit constraints (format, numbers)
- 2 = acceptable: correct, minor style/format issues
- 3 = ideal: correct, concise, follows constraints and matches examples

Notes on sampling: prefer seeded deterministic batches (seed=42) for bisecting regressions; randomize when exploring prevalence. Use length buckets: short (<40 tokens), medium (40-160), long (>160). Keep at least 6 samples per bucket.

2) Recent sample outputs (input -> model outputs) — reproducible example for ticket:
- Input A (short): "Summarize: 2-line bullet list of benefits of caching for LLMs."
  gptx-small: "Caching reduces repeated computation, speeds responses." (score: 2)
  gptx-small-quant: "Makes tokens faster. Less cost." (score: 1)
  Observation: quant variant dropped the terse structure and missed bullet formatting. Might be tokenizer truncation at low-prob contexts.

- Input B (medium): "Given a CSV row, output JSON schema with types. Row: \"42, 2023-11-12, True, 123.45\""
  gptx-small: Correct mapping to int/date/bool/float but used epoch for date (score: 2).
  gptx-small-quant: Returned strings for all fields (score: 0).
  Hypothesis: quantization affected calibration on less common tokens (digits + hyphen).

3) Regression signal properties I care about (notes-to-self):
- Hallucination spike correlated with short-range KV cache misses in streaming runs.
- Temperature changes (0.0 -> 0.2) amplify decoding instability for quant models more than fp16 models.
- Tokenizer boundary cases: long numeric sequences and backslash escapes show more variability after the latest kernel selector swap.
- Latency-steered fallback: when routing downgraded to cpu-fallback, quality drops but pattern differs between models; need separate baselines.

4) Minimal experiment plan to triage (next actions):
- Re-run 200-sample seeded check across length buckets with T=0.0 and T=0.2. Record divergence rate and top-token KL. (Assign: Mina)
- Create tiny binary A/B harness that logs tokenizer pre/post bytes for failing samples. (Assign: me)
- Run quantized model with pinned kernel-version (old selector) to see if regression is selector or quant profile. (Assign: Rajiv)
- If selector implicated, bisect commits between 2025-01-02 .. 2025-01-09 (fastest path).

5) Misc notes / heuristics I keep forgetting:
- Always include the exact prompt, including trailing newline and special whitespace, in tickets.
- When scoring, prefer absolute failure (0) vs grading on a gradient; makes triage filters easier.
- Use small human-readable labels for buckets in dashboards: s/m/l instead of token counts.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is there telemetry for per-request tokenizer bytes? (ask infra)
- Does the runtime log kernel selection reason on serving? (ask runtime infra)
- Consider an automated micro-eval job that runs every rollout and emits the 20-sample rubric snapshot to the rollout card.

One-off observations (2025-01-23): ran a quick noon probe — found 7/20 medium-length prompts scored 1 or 0 on quant variant. Flagged in JIRA-ML-1427. Adding this docket to ticket so reviewers can see my quick steps and sample lines.

Scratch log (random):
- 2025-01-08: noticed that when prompt ends with colon+newline, quant model sometimes continues in list form without punctuation.
- 2025-01-11: brief chat w/ Rajiv — agreed to run kernel pinned tests next week.

If I come back to this doc: paste output CSV from the harness here and convert to cheat-table for the ticket. Also, save one passing + one failing canonical sample to GDrive /shared_drives for reproducible artifacts.

End.
